newsitem.title: POLAND: POLISH POLAR EXPLORER SETS OUT TO CROSS ANTARCTICA.
newsitem.headline: POLISH POLAR EXPLORER SETS OUT TO CROSS ANTARCTICA.

text.p: Polish polar explorer Marek Kaminski flew to Chile on Monday where he will set out on a gruelling solitary trek across Antarctica, public television said.
He said he planned to embark on his 3,000-kilometre (nearly 2,000 miles) march from Berkner Island to the Ross Sea in late October or early November.

Poland's largest-selling daily Gazeta EWyborcza listed four other trekkers, who plan to set out at the same time, as Norwegian explorer Bourge Ousland, Briton Sir Ranluph Fiennes, Korean Cho Ouyo and an unnamed Frenchwomen.
"There is no rivalry involved, the Antarctic is no race course" Kaminski said. "Everyone is going because they love it very much and that's all there is to it."
Kaminski, who will pull a supply-sled weighing 200 kg (424 lbs), hopes to traverse the icy continent amid temperatures plunging to 50 below Celsius in three to four months' time.
No stranger to polar exploration, in 1995 Kaminski and a companion became the first Poles to walk to the North Pole.
Later that year, Kaminski embarked on a 53-day solitary march to the South Pole, becoming the first person ever to conquer both poles in a single year.
"I want to be there as long as possible, because that is where I feel the best. I simply love Antarctica," he told Gazeta.
